note: Examples are JSON because a channel spec is authored in YAML and validated after parsing; the schema sees the parsed document either way. All names, hosts and digests are synthetic. No example carries a payload, a record key or a credential value.
expectation_note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by qa-engineer with `contracts/validate.py --emit-expectations` against jsonschema Draft 2020-12, and independently by the lead (94 checks, 0 failed, first run). Every expected_json_path/expected_validator pair below is the failing location and keyword that example MUST produce, so an example that fails for the WRONG reason goes red instead of passing (code-reviewer Medium 2, Phase 0 gate). These 19 pairs were first written as architect predictions - this session has no shell - and all 19 matched the measured run exactly, including the three flagged as least certain; no correction was needed. Paths and keywords only, never instance values, so this file is PHI-safe. An example may fail on more than one pair; the test asserts the pinned pair is among the failures.
runnable_note: Every valid entry declares `runnable`. true means every step it names resolves in the shipping distribution TODAY, so a test may load and execute it. false means it illustrates a channel a later wave will make authorable, and `requires` lists the namespaces or mechanisms that do not exist yet, each with the task that delivers it. This is DATA rather than prose because the same classification is needed by the schema corpus test in tributary-runtime, and an allow-list duplicated in a test drifts from the contract that owns it. Three rules for whoever maintains that test: a `runnable: true` example whose steps stop resolving is a failure; a `runnable: false` example whose `requires` have ALL become resolvable is also a failure - the entry must then be promoted to true and its `requires` deleted, so a stale exemption cannot silently mask a real gap; and AT LEAST ONE entry must be `runnable: true`, because a corpus where every example is exempt no longer demonstrates that any channel spec can be executed at all, and would go green saying so. SET 1.1 ADDITION: `runnable` now covers CONNECTORS as well as steps. A `requires` entry of the form `connector:<source|destination>/<type> (task)` names a receiver or loader type that is in the schema but not yet shipped; such an example is not runnable however its steps resolve. The step-resolution test cannot see connectors, so it must treat a `connector:` entry as unresolved until the entry is deleted, and the owning engineer asks the architect to delete it when the connector ships with its duplicate-delivery test. Every set 1.1 example also names a `ref` step, so none can be promoted by W2-1 landing alone.

valid.note: Wave 1 E2E shape and the only currently runnable example: MLLP on loopback with no TLS, ordering none, HTTP stub on loopback, idempotency 'none' with the required justification. Its step uses `uses: tributary.core.passthrough`, an entry point in the running image, because `ref` needs bundle-fetch and that does not exist in wave 1 (README 3.3.1)
Production shape: wildcard bind with mTLS, per-key ordering, byte-bounded queue, three steps, HTTPS destination with blocking retry and halt-partition
The form on _tb.<env>.channels: metadata.version set by the control plane, partitions and retention overrides, transactional pipeline
Two destinations with different idempotency techniques and different exhaustion behaviour on one unordered channel

Set 1.1. Wave 2 exit criterion 1 shape: per-key MLLP with mTLS to a FHIR transaction destination, a ClickHouse row destination and an MLLP forward, each sink getting its own payload through destination steps
Set 1.1. HTTP/FHIR ingest with bearer auth over TLS, keyed by a JSON pointer, to a FHIR server and a PostgreSQL table
Set 1.1. SFTP poller with pinned host keys and move-after-commit, to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket and a second SFTP server, both named from tb-msg-id
Set 1.1. External Kafka source over SASL_SSL keyed by the inbound record key, to ClickHouse and to a partner cluster over mTLS with the key preserved

invalid.violates: spec.required: ordering. Invariant 5 - ordering is explicit, so there is no default
ordering per-key requires partitionKey; without it the runtime would have to invent a key or silently fall back to round-robin
ordering none must not carry partitionKey: a key expression that is silently ignored reads as ordered and is not
retry.policy retry-topic is DEFINED but not selectable in v0: never implemented or measured, and its delay mechanism is undecided (ADR-003 D1/D2, gate 7.2 item 18)
pipeline.bundle must be digest-pinned; a tag lets the code running in production change with no channel version to explain it
a listener on a non-loopback address (here 0.0.0.0) requires tls. Phase 1 requirement 8 (SR-8, CR-10) made enforceable rather than reviewed
tls.clientAuth must be stated, with no default: a default is the mTLS setting everyone inherits and nobody reviews
ack.mode is a one-member enum: after-commit. Invariant 1 - ACK timing is not a tuning knob, and 'on-receive' is the exact mistake the invariant exists to prevent
queue.maxBytes is required whenever queue is present; an item count is not a memory bound when an item can be 1 MB (Phase 1 requirement 5, SR-3)
a step has no field carrying inline code. Invariant 7 - a step must be a unit-testable function of (message, ctx), and inline source cannot be imported by pytest, reviewed in a diff or type-checked
exactly one of uses or ref; both means two candidate implementations and an undefined precedence
invalid.expectation_note: Shares its pinned pair with step-neither-uses-nor-ref.json: one oneOf covers both directions. Weak evidence of WHY, accepted for the same reason as the topic-name anyOf - splitting the schema would not distinguish them

invalid.violates: exactly one of uses or ref; neither leaves the step with no implementation to load
step.with rejects property names that denote a credential ('token'); secrets go through auth.secretRef and never into a spec
invalid.expectation_note: Measured. propertyNames reports at the containing object with the inner keyword, matching the events attrs deny-list precedent ($.attrs / not). If this ever reports 'pattern' instead, the example is failing on the name charset and the credential deny-list has stopped being tested

invalid.violates: plaintext http is permitted only to loopback; PHI in flight to a remote destination is TLS or it is a breach
a destination URL carries no query string: the identifier a healthcare API wants there is usually the record key, and a URL is logged by every proxy on the path (contracts/envelope/v0 section 4)
every destination declares its idempotency technique. Invariant 4 - at-least-once delivery means an undeclared technique is an undetected duplicate
technique 'none' requires a written justification a reviewer can read; it is allowed, unexplained it is not
spec.additionalProperties: an unrecognised key in a tenant-supplied document the data plane trusts completely is a typo or an injection, never a feature
metadata.name must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$: it becomes a topic segment and the tb-channel header, and Kafka metrics collapse '.' and are case-sensitive
an http source must state auth.type, with no default - the same rule as tls.clientAuth
